Levels.Chewing-artifact: Artifact from moving the jaw in a chewing motion.
Levels.ECG-artifact: An electrical artifact from the far-field potential from pulsation of the heart, time locked to QRS complex.
Levels.EMG-artifact: Artifact from muscle activity and myogenic potentials at the measurements site. In EEG, myogenic potentials are the most common artifacts. Frontalis and temporalis muscles (e.g. clenching of jaw muscles) are common causes. Generally, the potentials generated in the muscles are of shorter duration than those generated in the brain. The frequency components are usually beyond 30-50 Hz, and the bursts are arrhythmic.
Levels.Eye-blink-artifact: Artifact from eye blinking. In EEG, Fp1/Fp2 electrodes become electro-positive with eye closure because the cornea is positively charged causing a negative deflection in Fp1/Fp2. If the eye blink is unilateral, consider prosthetic eye.
Levels.Horizontal-eye-movement-artifact: Artifact from moving eyes left-to-right and right-to-left. In EEG, there is an upward deflection in the Fp2-F8 derivation, when the eyes move to the right side. In this case F8 becomes more positive and therefore. When the eyes move to the left, F7 becomes more positive and there is an upward deflection in the Fp1-F7 derivation.
Levels.Slow-eye-movement-artifact: Artifacts originating from slow, rolling eye-movements, seen during drowsiness.
Levels.Vertical-eye-movement-artifact: Artifact from moving eyes up and down. In EEG, this causes positive potentials (50-100 micro V) with bi-frontal distribution, maximum at Fp1 and Fp2, when the eyeball rotates upward. The downward rotation of the eyeball is associated with the negative deflection. The time course of the deflections is similar to the time course of the eyeball movement.
Levels.Movement-artifact: Artifact in the measured data generated by motion of the subject.
Levels.Pulse-artifact: A mechanical artifact from a pulsating blood vessel near a measurement site, cardio-ballistic artifact.
Levels.Sweat-artifact: Artifact from sweating. In EEG, this is a low amplitude undulating waveform that is usually greater than 2 seconds and may appear to be an unstable baseline.
Levels.Tongue-movement-artifact: Artifact from tongue movement (Glossokinetic). The tongue functions as a dipole, with the tip negative with respect to the base. In EEG, the artifact produced by the tongue has a broad potential field that drops from frontal to occipital areas, although it is less steep than that produced by eye movement artifacts. The amplitude of the potentials is greater inferiorly than in parasagittal regions; the frequency is variable but usually in the delta range. Chewing and sucking can produce similar artifacts.
Levels.Induction-artifact: Artifacts induced by nearby equipment. In EEG, these are usually of high frequency.
Levels.Electrode-pops-artifact: Brief artifact with a steep rise and slow fall of an electrophysiological signal, most often caused by a loose electrode.
Levels.Salt-bridge-artifact: Artifact from salt-bridge between EEG electrodes.

value.Description: Marker code written by the recording system

sample.Description: Onset as a 0-based sample index relative to the first sample in the data file.

channels.Description: For rows with event_source 'electroclean_artifact': a JSON array of channel names. An empty array [] means the artifact affects the whole recording montage (all channels). Original rows have n/a (no channel information in the original events).

Levels.original:events_tsv: Unchanged row from the recording's original BIDS events.tsv.
Levels.original:brainvision_vmrk: Marker from the BrainVision .vmrk file (read with MNE-Python).

annotation_id.Description: Stable identifier of the ElectroClean artifact annotation (n/a for original rows).

annotator_id.Description: Identifier of the annotator who created the artifact annotation (n/a for original rows).

original_row.Description: 1-based row number in the original events file (n/a for artifact rows).

time_conventions.onset: Seconds from the first sample stored in the data file (BIDS events.tsv convention; equal to MNE raw.times).
time_conventions.sample: 0-based sample index relative to the first stored sample: sample = onset * sfreq.
time_conventions.interval: Half-open: an annotation covers samples [onset_sample, onset_sample + duration_samples).
time_conventions.boundary_snapping: Boundaries are snapped to the nearest sample when created or edited.
time_conventions.mne_annotations: In mne.Annotations attached to Raw, onset_mne = onset + first_samp / sfreq (relative to orig_time).
